newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU proposes most euro coins be nickel free.
newsitem.headline: EU proposes most euro coins be nickel free.

text.p: The European Commission, responding to health concerns, proposed on Thursday that six out of the planned eight euro coins should not include nickel.
It also called for various design features to be included included grooves and edgings to allow the blind to identify the money.

The European Union executive said the proposal meant that 92 percent of the coins in circulation from, in principle, the beginning of 2002, would be nickel free compared to 25 percent in today's national currencies.
There are some 70 billion coins in circulation in the 15 EU nations.
Sweden has been most critical of the use of nickel in the future European currency arguing that it may cause allergies.
The Commission said it proposed using a nickel-free alloy, Nordic gold, for the 10, 20 and 50 cent coins and the one, two and five cent coins would also be nickel free.
But with current technology it would be difficult to develop an alternative to nickel for the one and two euro coins.
It said it would continue research but "meanwhile, the Commission proposes that the coins of one and two euros be produced using technology which maintains the use of nickel".
Nordic Gold has no gold in it despite the name. It consists mainly of copper and is produced by Finnish metal group Outokumpu.
France is a major nickel producer through its New Caledonia territory in the South Pacific where the Eramet mining group is a large player
But Sweden was apparently successful in persuading the Commission to cut back sharply on the use of the nickel

Its finance ministry has cited figures showing that 20 percent of young women in Europe are affected by nickel allergy, partly because of frequent exposure to the metal, for example by wearing earrings and other jewellery.
The Commission proposals need the backing of EU finance ministers.
